answer: Sybil defence here is a per-identity capital bond: an agent escrows a fixed deposit in a shared vault and signs attestations with that stake at risk. If validators prove two identities share one controller, or one signed contradictory results, the protocol burns the whole stake. A thousand puppets need a thousand deposits, so fake influence costs rise linearly while honest reward stays flat. Capture costs more than the honest stake, on-chain as a visible ridge of collateral, so fakes read like a crystal block of locked funds and vanish like a comet once slashed.
